title: Closed-Loop Active Learning Discovers Novel Ultra-Low-Expansion High-Entropy Invar Alloys
whyItMatters: A generative active-learning loop screened millions of sparse multi-element alloy compositions—synthesizing only 17 candidates—to discover two novel high-entropy Invar alloys with record-low thermal expansion (~2 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹).
summary: Published in Science in October 2022 by Ziyuan Rao, Po-Yen Tung, Ruiwen Xie, Fritz Körmann, Dierk Raabe, and colleagues at the Max-Planck-Institut für Eisenforschung (MPIE) and TU Darmstadt, this work combined a generative Wasserstein autoencoder, ensemble neural networks, density functional theory, thermodynamic modeling, and metallurgical synthesis in a six-iteration closed active-learning loop. Searching millions of candidate Fe–Ni–Co–Cr multi-principal-element compositions from very sparse experimental data, the system required synthesizing and characterizing only 17 new alloys to discover two previously unknown high-entropy Invar alloys exhibiting ultra-low thermal expansion coefficients near 2 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ across wide temperature ranges.
technicalHighlights: Combined a Wasserstein autoencoder (HEA-GAD) with ensemble neural predictors, DFT magnetic-moment calculations, and CALPHAD thermodynamics in six closed experimental loops.
Pinpointed two novel high-entropy Invar alloys with thermal expansion coefficients ~2 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 300 K after testing just 17 synthesized compositions out of millions.
Uncovered a physics-informed magnetic descriptor governing the Invar anomaly in concentrated solid-solution alloys.
caveats: Each experimental iteration still required manual arc-melting, homogenization, and dilatometry characterization by metallurgists; scaling to broader mechanical/corrosion multi-objective alloy design requires richer high-throughput characterization.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated generative active learning conquering sparse-data, high-dimensional multi-principal-element metallurgy where empirical rules fail.
scoreRationale.ripple: Provided a widely replicated blueprint for AI-guided discovery of sustainable structural, magnetic, and cryogenic high-entropy alloys.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science with physical synthesis, microstructural characterization, and dilatometry confirming both novel Invar alloys.
scoreRationale.velocity: Navigated millions of candidate alloy compositions to two record-performing physical alloys in just 17 experimental trials.
